questions.q: A long straight wire of radius a carries a steady current I. The current is uniformly distributed across its cross section. The ratio of the magnetic field at $\frac{a}{2}$ and $2 a$ from axis of the wire is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{B}_1 2 \pi \frac{\mathrm{a}}{2}=\mu_{\mathrm{o}} \frac{\mathrm{I}}{4} \\ & \mathrm{~B}_1=\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{o}} \mathrm{I}}{4 \pi \mathrm{a}} \\ & \mathrm{B}_2 2 \pi 2 \mathrm{a}=\mu_{\mathrm{o}} \mathrm{I} \\ & \mathrm{B}_2=\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{o}} \mathrm{I}}{4 \pi \mathrm{a}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
An electron is moving along the positive x-axis. If uniform magnetic field is applied parallel to the negative z-axis, then

A.The electron will experience magnetic force along positive y-axis

B.The electron will experience magnetic force along negative y-axis

C.The electron will not experience any force in magnetic field

D.The electron will continue to move along the positive x-axis

E.The electron will move along circular path in magnetic field

Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The Lorentz force is given by

F→=qv→×B→

=-ev→×B→

So, F^=i^×k^=-j^.

F→ is  along -y axis 

As the magnetic field is perpendicular to the velocity, motion would be circular.

questions.q:
A wire X of length 50 cm carrying a current of 2 A is placed parallel to a long wire Y of length 5 m. The wire Y carries a current of 3 A. The distance between two wires is 5 cm and currents flow in the same direction. The force acting on the wire Y is :

​​​​​​​
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
An attractive force will act normal to  X towards Y because the direction of the currents in the wires is the same.

Force exerted on length l due to the magnetic field is given as F=FXY=FYX=I1l1 B12

⇒F=μ0I1I22πrl1

Given here, I1=2 A, I2= 3 A, l1=5 m, r=5 cm.

Putting the values, we have

F=4π×10-7×2×32π×5×10-2×50×10-2

=1.2×10-5 N directed towards wire X.

questions.q: An iron rod of volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math> and relative permeability <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn></math> is placed as core in a solenoid with<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>turns</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> . If a current of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is passed through the solenoid, then the magnetic moment of the rod will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,

Volume of iron rod is, V=10-3 m3

Relative permeability, μr=1000

No of turns per unit length of solenoid is, n=Nl=10 turns cm-1=1000 turns m-1

Current through the solenoid is, i=0.5 A

Magnetic moment of an iron core solenoid is given by,

M=(μr-1) NiA

⇒M=μr-1NiVl=μr-1NliV

⇒M=1000-1×1000×0.5×10-3

⇒M=499.5≈500 A m2

questions.q: Two magnetic dipoles X and Y are placed at a separation d , with their axes perpendicular to each other. The dipole moment of Y is twice that of X . A particle of charge q is passing through their mid-point P , at angle θ=45o with the horizontal line, as shown in figure. What would be the magnitude of force on the particle at that instant? ( d is much larger than the dimension of the dipole)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
BX=2μ04πMd/2 along x -axis
BY=μ04π2Md/2 along y -axis
BX=BY

Hence Bnet will be at 45o from x -axis.
Now, velocity and magnetic field are in same direction. Hence no force will act on the particle.

questions.q: N equally spaced charges each of value q , are placed on a circle of radius R . The circle rotates about its axis with an angular velocity $\omega$ as shown in the figure. A bigger Amperian loop B encloses the whole circle where as a smaller Amperian loop A encloses a small segment. The difference between enclosed currents, $I_A-I_B$, for the given Amperian loops is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & I_A=\frac{N q}{\frac{2 \pi}{\omega}} \\ & I_A=\frac{N q \omega}{2 \pi}, I_B=0 \\ & I_A=I_B=\frac{N q \omega}{2 \pi}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Magnetic fields at two points on the axis of a circular coil at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>05</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> from the centre are in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. The radius of coil is _______ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know, the magnetic field on the axis of a current carrying circular ring is given by

B=μ04π2NIAR2+x23/2

∴  B1 B2=81=R2+0.22R2+0.0523/2

4R2+0.052=R2+0.22

4R2-R2=0.22-4×0.052

4R2-R2=0.22-0.12

3R2=0.3×0.1

R2=0.12⇒R=0.1

questions.q: Two ions of masses 4 amu  and 16 amu have charges +2 e and +3 e respectively. These ions pass through the region of the constant perpendicular magnetic field. The kinetic energy of both ions is the same. Then:
options: lighter ion will be deflected less than heavier ion
lighter ion will be deflected more than heavier ion
both ions will be deflected equally
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The relation between linear moment and radius in terms of the magnitude of magnetic field and charge of a particle, r=PqB=2mkeqB

⇒r∝mq⇒r1r2=34⇒r2>r1.

questions.q:
A massless square loop, of wire of resistance 10 Ω, supporting a mass of 1 g, hangs vertically with one of its sides in a uniform magnetic field of 103 G, directed outwards in the shaded region. A dc voltage V is applied to the loop. For what value of V, the magnetic force will exactly balance the weight of the supporting mass of 1 g?

(If sides of the loop = 10 cm, g=10 m s-2)

.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For balancing of force, 

Magnetic force Fm=weight of supporting mass mg.

∴ILB=mg

∴VRLB=mg     ∵From Ohm's law, I=VR

∴V=mgRLB

=1×10-3 kg10 m s-210 Ω0.1 m103×10-4 T=10 V

Statement (I) : When currents vary with time, Newton's third law is valid only if momentum carried by the electromagnetic field is taken into account.
Statement (II) : Ampere's circuital law does not depend on Biot-Savart's law.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q:
Given below two statements : One is labelled as Assertion (A) and other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Non-polar materials do not have any permanent dipole moment.

Reason (R): When a non-polar material is placed in an electric field, the centre of the positive charge distribution of it's individual atom or molecule coincides with the centre of the negative charge distribution.

In the light of above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Non-polar materials do not have any permanent dipole moment. This statement is true.

When a non-polar material is placed in an electric field, centre of positive charge is pushed in the direction of the electric field and centre of the negative charge is pushed in the direction opposite to the electric field. Hence, they don't coincide. Therefore, reason is false.

questions.q:
In a moving coil galvanometer, two moving coils $M_1$ and $M_2$ have the following particulars :
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{R}_1=5 \Omega, \mathrm{~N}_1=15, \mathrm{~A}_1=3.6 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^2, \mathrm{~B}_1=0.25 \mathrm{~T} \\ & \mathrm{R}_2=7 \Omega, \mathrm{~N}_2=21, \mathrm{~A}_2=1.8 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^2, \mathrm{~B}_2=0.50 \mathrm{~T}
\end{aligned}$
Assuming that torsional constant of the springs are same for both coils, what will be the ratio of voltage sensitivity of $M_1$ and $M_2$ ?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Voltage sensitivity }=\frac{\theta}{V}=\frac{N A B}{c R} \\ & \text { Ratio }==\left(\frac{\mathrm{N}_1 \mathrm{~A}_1 \mathrm{~B}_1}{\mathrm{~N}_2 \mathrm{~A}_2 \mathrm{~B}_2}\right) \frac{\mathrm{R}_2}{\mathrm{R}_1}=\frac{15 \times 3.6 \times 0.25}{21 \times 1.8 \times 0.5} \times \frac{7}{5}=\frac{1}{1}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A charge particle moving in magnetic field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mo>,</mo></math> has the components of velocity along <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> as well as perpendicular to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math>. The path of the charge particle will be
options: helical path with the axis perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math>
helical path with the axis along magnetic field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math>
straight along the direction of magnetic field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the radius of the path followed by the charged particle under an external magnetic field can be written as

r=mvBq   ...1

The perpendicular component of velocity results in circular motion, while the parallel component results in linear motion. Hence, the path of the charged particle is helical in nature, the axis of which lies along the direction of the magnetic field.

questions.q: An element $\Delta l=\Delta x \hat{i}$ is placed at the origin and carries a large current $I=10 \mathrm{~A}$. The magnetic field on the $y$-axis at a distance of $0.5 \mathrm{~m}$ from the elements $\Delta x$ of $1 \mathrm{~cm}$ length is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{dB}} & =\frac{\mu_0 \mathrm{I}}{4 \pi} \frac{(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{d} l} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}})}{\mathrm{r}^3}(\text { Tesla) } \\ & =\frac{10^{-7} \times 10 \times\left(\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{100}\right)(+\hat{\mathrm{k}})}{\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3}=4 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{~T}(+\hat{\mathrm{k}})\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A magnetic dipole experiences a torque of $80 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~N} \mathrm{~m}$ when placed in uniform magnetic field in such a way that dipole moment makes angle of $60^{\circ}$ with magnetic field. The potential energy of the dipole is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\tau=\mathrm{M} \times \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{MB} \sin 60=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \mathrm{MB}=80 \sqrt{3}$
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{MB}=160 \\ & \mathrm{U}=-\mathrm{M} \cdot \mathrm{B}=-\mathrm{MB} \cos 60 \\ & \mathrm{U}=-160 \times 1 / 2=-80 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A solenoid of length $0.5 \mathrm{~m}$ has a radius of $1 \mathrm{~cm}$ and is made up of ' $\mathrm{m}$ ' number of turns. It carries a current of $5 \mathrm{~A}$. If the magnitude of the magnetic field inside the solenoid is $6.28 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~T}$ then the value of $m$ is _____.

questions.solution:
$\mu_0 n i=B \quad n=$ number of turns per unit length
$\mu_0\left(\frac{\mathrm{m}}{\ell}\right) \mathrm{i}=\mathrm{B}\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{m}=\frac{B . \ell}{\mu_0 \mathrm{i}}=\frac{6.28 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.5}{12.56 \times 10^{-7} \times 5} \\ & \mathrm{~m}=500\end{aligned}$

questions.q: An electron in a hydrogen atom revolves around its nucleus with a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>76</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> in an orbit of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>52</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Å</mi></math>. The magnetic field produced at the nucleus of the hydrogen atom is _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The magnetic field due to the electron is given by 

B=μ0qvsin90°4πr2

The given data is 

v=6.76×106 m s-1r=0.52×10-10 m

Thus, the magnetic field is 

B=10-7×1.6××10-19×6.76×1060.52×0.52×10-20=40 T
